newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada natives to protest until Chretien meeting.
newsitem.headline: Canada natives to protest until Chretien meeting.

text.p: Canada's top native leader, Ovide Mercredi, said on Friday that Indians would escalate their political demonstrations until Prime Minister Jean Chretien agreed to meet to discuss their concerns.

Mercredi and other native Indian chiefs held a sit-in at Chretien's office block on Thursday afternoon to demand a meeting, ending it when an official promised Chretien would respond in writing on Friday.

Mercredi said Chretien wrote him with bland generalities reaffirming his commitment to reviewing a major report by the Royal Commission on Aboriginal Peoples (RCAP), but without a promise for a meeting.
"I am very disappointed that the prime minister is dismissing the simple request to meet with us and is thereby ignoring our demands for reform in this country," Mercredi told a news conference.

Canadian native Indians have the highest rates of poverty, suicide, substance abuse and incarceration in the country, and the Royal Commission made 440 recommendations for improvement -- from giving them more control over their land to establishing a native legislative chamber.
"The federal government is committed to reviewing the RCAP report and recommendations. The report is comprehensive and deserves serious consideration," Chretien said in his letter.
But he said time was needed to deal with the problems and there was no quick fix.
Mercredi, formally called the national chief of the Assembly of First Nations, said provincial premiers and high-ranking organisational leaders would have been met by now.
"When your chief whom you've elected to represent you at the national level, cannot even get a meeting with the prime minister, it humiliates the people that you represent," he said.

The native demonstrations will target Chretien and other influential political figures, whose public appearances will be followed closely, Mercredi said, yet refusing to reveal what form the protests will take.

He said the demonstrations will stop when Chretien and the federal government agree to meet on an ongoing basis with the native leaders to try to reach consensus on the Royal Commission recommendations.
